title: strictNullChecks and the null safety model
hook: With strictNullChecks enabled, null and undefined are their own types — not assignable to string or number unless you opt in. It is compile-time only: JSON, Redis, and fetch still deliver null at runtime, so you narrow or validate at boundaries like C# nullable reference types.

blocks.text: **strictNullChecks** is a compiler flag (part of **strict**) that makes **null** and **undefined** distinct types. A variable typed `string` cannot hold `null` unless you write `string | null`. Optional properties (`email?`) include `undefined` in their type. **Control-flow narrowing** after `if (x !== null)` refines the type inside the block. This is **compile-time only** — emitted JavaScript is unchanged; runtime null still crashes if you skip checks.

entries.plainDefinition: When true, null and undefined are not assignable to other types by default.
Explicitly documents that a value may be absent.
Short-circuit property access when intermediate is null/undefined.
Default only for null/undefined — not other falsy values.

blocks.text: Before strictNullChecks, `users.find()` returning undefined and accessing `.name` compiled fine — classic production bug. Enabling it on legacy codebases surfaces thousands of errors that reflect real null risks. C# **nullable reference types (NRT)** are the cousin: `string` vs `string?` at compile time, both still null at runtime if you lie. Reddit senior threads rank strictNullChecks vs C# NRT as a frequent comparison — both need discipline at API boundaries.

blocks.title: strictNullChecks does not fix runtime
blocks.body: await redis.get(key) returns string | null in types only if you typed the client — runtime null still needs an if check.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Model absence explicitly
items.body: Use T | null | undefined on APIs that can miss.

items.title: Narrow before use
items.body: if (value != null) { ... } — compiler knows value is T.

items.title: Optional chaining for drill-down
items.body: obj?.nested?.field — undefined if any hop is nullish.

items.title: Validate external data
items.body: unknown + type guard — strictNullChecks does not parse JSON.

blocks.title: Confusing ?? with ||
blocks.body: || treats 0 and '' as falsy. ?? only null/undefined — use ?? for defaults on nullable strings and numbers.

blocks.title: Disabling strict to ship
blocks.body: Turning off strictNullChecks hides real bugs — fix with narrowing and explicit unions instead.

blocks.text: Compare strictNullChecks to C# NRT: both optional on legacy projects, both on in modern templates, neither prevents malicious JSON. exactOptionalPropertyTypes (separate flag) distinguishes missing prop from prop: undefined. definiteAssignmentAnalysis for class fields. Senior answer: enable strict early, use unknown at boundaries, never blanket !. Migration strategy: enable per-module with project references.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying strictNullChecks prevents runtime null. Using ! everywhere. Confusing optional ? with nullable | null. Not knowing C# NRT is compile-time too.

interviewTakeaways: strictNullChecks: null/undefined not assignable unless union or optional.
Narrow with if, ?., ?? — compiler tracks control flow.
Compile-time only — validate JSON/Redis/fetch at runtime.
60s: strictNullChecks separates null from string. Narrow before use. ?? not ||. Same idea as C# NRT — compile time not runtime. Boundaries still need guards.
commonPitfalls: Weak: strictNullChecks fixes runtime null — it does not.
Weak: ! on every nullable — assertion abuse.
Strong: 'Union with null, narrow at boundary, ?. and ?? for access. C# NRT parallel. unknown guard for JSON.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript has two nullish values — strictNullChecks forces you to model both; optional chaining and ?? are shared runtime syntax.
strictNullChecks handles internal null flow; unknown + guards handle external JSON that may omit or null any field.
